title: Checkpoint 3.1: sorry I'm late, guys
goal: Checkpoint: turn up late to meet Sēf and Fahad, say sorry to the group and swap stories about what everyone was doing
tip: To a group, the past progressive takes the group forms: kintu + verb 'you (all) were …-ing', kinna gāʿdīn 'we were …-ing', gimtu tiẓḥakūn 'you started laughing'. Say sorry to everyone with sāmḥūni. Participles take -a and -īn: mayyit, mayyta, mayytīn min iẓ-ẓiḥik 'dying of laughter'.
grammar: checkpoint 3.1: recycle s3u001–s3u011 (participles, kān gāʿid, gām + verb)
dialogue: A
وينك يا ريّال؟ كنا قاعدين نترياك!
wēnak yā rayyāl? kinna gāʿdīn nitrayyāk!
Where've you been, man? We've been sitting here waiting for you!
B
سامحوني شباب. كنت نايم وما سمعت التلفون
sāmḥūni shabāb. kint nāyim w ma simaʿt it-tilifōn
Sorry, guys. I was asleep and didn't hear the phone.
A
نايم للحين؟ شو كنت قاعد تسوي البارحة؟
nāyim lil-ḥīn? shu kint gāʿid tsawwi l-bārḥa?
Still asleep at this time? What were you doing last night?
B
كنت قاعد أذاكر لين الساعة ثنتين. وانتو، شو كنتوا تسوون؟
kint gāʿid adhākir lēn is-sāʿa thintēn. w intu, shu kintu tsawwūn?
I was revising till two. And you lot, what have you been up to?
A
فهد كان قاعد يسولف، وأنا ميت من الضحك!
Fahad kān gāʿid ysōlif, w ana mayyit min iẓ-ẓiḥik!
Fahad was telling stories, and I was dying of laughter!
B
صج؟ شو صار له؟
ṣij? shu ṣār-lah?
Really? What happened to him?
A
نام في المترو، ووصل آخر محطة!
nām fi l-mitrō, w wiṣal ākhir maḥaṭṭa!
He fell asleep on the metro and ended up at the last stop!
B
مسكين! وانتو قمتوا تضحكون عليه؟
maskīn! w intu gimtu tiẓḥakūn ʿalēh?
Poor guy! And you lot started laughing at him?
items: to one man: sāmiḥni (سامحني); to one woman: sāmḥīni (سامحيني)
we were (sitting here) waiting for you (to a man)
to a woman: kinna gāʿdīn nitrayyāch (كنا قاعدين نترياج)
what were you doing? what have you been up to? (to a group)
to one man: shu kint tsawwi?; to one woman: shu kinti tsawwīn?
dying of laughter, in stitches (a man)
a woman: mayyta min iẓ-ẓiḥik (ميتة من الضحك); a group: mayytīn min iẓ-ẓiḥik
about a woman: shu ṣār-lha? (شو صار لها؟)
you (all) started laughing, you burst out laughing
he started laughing: gām yiẓḥak (قام يضحك); we started: gimna (قمنا)

title: If you finish early, come straight over
goal: Plan a match night at Sēf's: say what happens if you finish early, run late or something comes up
tip: For a real 'if' or 'when' about the future, use idha + a past verb: idha khallaṣt badri 'if I finish early', idha taʼakhkhart 'if I'm late'. The verb looks past, but the meaning is future. The other half is a b- future or a command: idha ṣār shay, khabbirni 'if anything comes up, let me know'.
grammar: idha + past verb for a real 'if' about the future (idha khallaṣt, taʿāl)
dialogue: A
الليلة المباراة. بتيي تشوفها ويانا عندي؟
il-lēla l-mubārā. bitiyi tshūfha wiyyāna ʿindi?
The match is tonight. Are you coming to watch it with us at mine?
B
ودي، بس عندي دوام لين الساعة ثمان
widdi, bas ʿindi dawām lēn is-sāʿa thamān
I'd like to, but I'm at work till eight.
A
عادي. إذا خلصت بدري، تعال على طول
ʿādi. idha khallaṣt badri, taʿāl ʿala ṭūl
No problem. If you finish early, come straight over.
B
زين. وإذا تأخرت، بدق عليك
zēn. w idha taʼakhkhart, badigg ʿalēk
OK. And if I'm running late, I'll give you a ring.
A
ماشي. وإذا صار شي، خبرني
māshi. w idha ṣār shay, khabbirni
Fine. And if anything comes up, let me know.
B
إن شاء الله. وإذا ييت، أييب شي وياي؟
in shāʼ allāh. w idha yīt, ayīb shay wiyyāy?
Will do. And when I come, shall I bring anything?
A
هيه، ييب لنا عصير. وإذا وصلت، دق علي
hē, yīb-lna ʿaṣīr. w idha wiṣalt, digg ʿalay
Yes, bring us some juice. And when you get here, give me a ring.
B
ولا يهمك. أشوفك الليلة!
wala yhimmak. ashūfak il-lēla!
No problem. See you tonight!
items: if I finish, when I'm done; if you finish (to a man)
to a woman: idha khallaṣti (إذا خلصتي)
if I'm late; if you're late (to a man)
to a woman: idha taʼakhkharti (إذا تأخرتي)
I'll ring you, I'll call you (to a man)
to a woman: badigg ʿalēch (بدق عليج)
if anything comes up, if anything happens
let me know, tell me (to a man)
to a woman: khabbrīni (خبريني); to a group: khabbrūni (خبروني)
when I come, if I come; if you come (to a man)
to a woman: idha yīti (إذا ييتي)
when you get here, if you arrive (to a man); when I arrive
to a woman: idha wiṣalti (إذا وصلتي)
I'm at work, I've got work (that day)
ʿindi dawām lēn is-sāʿa thamān = I'm at work till eight

title: If it's no trouble, send me the file
goal: Offer Maryam a hand at the office when she's swamped, and make your offers and requests polite with idha
tip: When the condition is a want, a 'have' or how things are now, idha takes a present verb or ʿind-: idha tabīn 'if you'd like (to a woman)', idha ʿindak wagt 'if you've got time'. idha ma ʿalēch amr 'if it's no trouble (to a woman)' makes any request softer.
grammar: idha + present verb or ʿind- (idha tabīn, idha ʿindak wagt)
culture: At work, a request to a colleague is usually softened: idha ma ʿalēk amr, law samaḥt or mumkin…? before the verb. A bare command (ṭarrish-li l-malaff) can sound bossy, even between equals; with a friend it's fine.
dialogue: B
مريم، شكلج تعبانة. عندج شغل وايد؟
Maryam, shaklich taʿbāna. ʿindich shughul wāyid?
Maryam, you look tired. Have you got loads of work?
A
هيه والله. لازم أخلص العرض اليوم
hē wallāh. lāzim akhalliṣ il-ʿarẓ il-yōm
Yes, honestly. I have to finish the presentation today.
B
إذا تبين، أساعدج
idha tabīn, asāʿdich
If you like, I'll help you.
A
مشكور! إذا عندك وقت، شوف هالأرقام. أنا مب فاهمة شي
mashkūr! idha ʿindak wagt, shūf hal-argām. ana mub fāhma shay
Thanks! If you've got time, look at these figures. I can't make sense of them.
B
ماشي. وإذا لقيت شي غلط، أقول لج؟
māshi. w idha ligēt shay ghalaṭ, agūl-lich?
Sure. And if I find anything wrong, shall I tell you?
A
أكيد. بس إذا ما عندك وقت، مب مشكلة
akīd. bas idha ma ʿindak wagt, mub mushkila
Of course. But if you haven't got time, no problem.
B
عندي وقت. إذا ما عليج أمر، طرشي لي الملف
ʿindi wagt. idha ma ʿalēch amr, ṭarrshī-li l-malaff
I've got time. If it's no trouble, send me the file.
A
زين، الحين أطرش لك
zēn, il-ḥīn aṭarrish-lak
Great, I'll send it to you now.
items: to a man: shaklak taʿbān (شكلك تعبان)
have you got loads of work? (to a woman)
to a man: ʿindak shughul wāyid? (عندك شغل وايد؟)
I'll help you, let me help you (to a woman)
if you've got time (to a man)
to a woman: idha ʿindich wagt (إذا عندج وقت)
shall I tell you? (to a woman)
if it's no trouble, if you don't mind (to a woman)
to a man: idha ma ʿalēk amr (إذا ما عليك أمر)

title: Let's leave early, or we won't find a spot
goal: Plan a winter night in the desert with Sēf and the guys: what you'll do if things go wrong, and what happens otherwise
tip: idha ma + past verb means 'if … not': idha ma ligēna 'if we don't find (one)'. willa means 'or else, otherwise': lāzim niṭlaʿ badri, willa ma binilga makān 'we have to leave early, or we won't find a spot'. Don't mix it up with walla 'or' in questions.
culture: In the cooler months, roughly November to March, going to il-barr is a favourite outing: friends or families drive out to the desert, put up a tent, light a fire, make coffee and often stay till morning. Popular spots fill up fast at weekends.
dialogue: A
شباب، شو رأيكم نروح البر يوم الجمعة؟
shabāb, shu raʼykum nrūḥ il-barr yōm il-jumʿa?
Guys, how about going to the desert on Friday?
B
فكرة حلوة! وإذا ما عندكم شي، نقعد لين الصبح
fikra ḥilwa! w idha ma ʿindakum shay, nigʿid lēn iṣ-ṣubḥ
Great idea! And if you've got nothing on, we can stay till morning.
A
زين. بس عندكم خيمة؟ أنا ما عندي
zēn. bas ʿindakum khēma? ana ma ʿindi
OK. But have you got a tent? I haven't.
B
لا. إذا ما لقينا، نشتري وحدة
la. idha ma ligēna, nishtiri waḥda
No. If we can't find one, we'll buy one.
A
ماشي. ولازم نطلع بدري، وإلا ما بنلقى مكان
māshi. w lāzim niṭlaʿ badri, willa ma binilga makān
Fine. And we have to leave early, or else we won't find a spot.
B
صح. وإذا الجو بارد في الليل؟
ṣaḥḥ. w idha l-jaww bārid fi l-lēl?
True. And what if it's cold at night?
A
كل واحد ييب بطانية، وإلا بنموت من البرد!
kill wāḥid yīb baṭṭāniyya, willa binmūt min il-bard!
Everyone bring a blanket, or else we'll freeze!
B
وأنا بييب الحطب والدلة
w ana bayīb il-ḥaṭab w id-dalla
And I'll bring the firewood and the coffee pot.
items: idha ma ligēna = if we don't find (one)
if you've got nothing on, if you're free (to a group)
to one man: idha ma ʿindak shay; to one woman: idha ma ʿindich shay
if we don't find (one), if we can't find (one)
not the same as walla (ولّا) 'or' in questions
we won't find a spot, there'll be no room for us
we'll freeze (lit. we'll die of the cold)

title: If I had a million
goal: Dream out loud with Sēf at a car showroom: what you'd each do if you had the money
tip: lō is the 'if' of things that aren't true or probably won't happen: lō ʿindi flūs 'if I had money'. The result takes chān + a past verb, and chān never changes: lō ʿindi malyōn, chān riḥt kill makān 'if I had a million, I'd go everywhere'. Real, likely plans keep idha.
grammar: lō for an imagined 'if'; result with chān + past (lō ʿindi …, chān …)
dialogue: A
شايف هالسيارة؟ لو عندي فلوس، جان اشتريتها اليوم
shāyif has-sayyāra? lō ʿindi flūs, chān ishtarēt-ha l-yōm
See this car? If I had the money, I'd buy it today.
B
كم سعرها؟
cham siʿirha?
How much is it?
A
مليون ونص!
malyōn w nuṣṣ!
One and a half million!
B
لو عندي مليون، جان رحت كل مكان في الدنيا
lō ʿindi malyōn, chān riḥt kill makān fi d-dinya
If I had a million, I'd go everywhere in the world.
A
وأنا لو عندي مليون، جان اشتريت بيت حق أمي
w ana lō ʿindi malyōn, chān ishtarēt bēt ḥagg ummi
And if I had a million, I'd buy my mum a house.
B
حلو! بس لو تدري، أنا ما عندي ولا فلس
ḥilu! bas lō tadri, ana ma ʿindi wala fils
Nice! But if only you knew, I haven't got a penny.
A
وأنا بعد! يلا عيل، الكرك علي
w ana baʿad! yalla ʿayal, il-karak ʿalay
Same here! Come on then, the karak's on me.
B
لو عندك مليون، جان الغدا بعد عليك!
lō ʿindak malyōn, chān il-ghada baʿad ʿalēk!
If you had a million, lunch would be on you too!
items: for a real, likely 'if' use idha (إذا); the phrase law samaḥt keeps law
lō ʿindi wagt = if I had time
to a woman: lō ʿindich (لو عندج)
I'd buy it, I would have bought it (a feminine thing, such as a car)
for a masculine thing: chān ishtarētah (جان اشتريته)
I'd go, I would have gone
chān never changes: chān riḥna = we'd go
malyōn w nuṣṣ = one and a half million
if only you knew (to a man)
to a woman: lō tadrīn (لو تدرين)
not a penny, not a single fils
a fils is a hundredth of a dirham

title: If I were you, I'd say yes
goal: Sēf has a job offer in Abu Dhabi and isn't sure: give him advice with lō and wish him luck
tip: lō ana makānak 'if I were you' is the usual way to give advice, and the advice follows with chān + past: lō ana makānak, chān wāfagt 'if I were you, I'd say yes'. With a present verb, lō is a gentle 'if': lō tishraḥ-lah, yimkin ywāfig 'if you explained it to him, he might agree'.
grammar: lō in advice and wishes (lō ana makānak, yā lēt)
culture: Many Muslims avoid lō when regretting the past ('if only I'd…'), following a well-known hadith that says 'if' opens the door to the devil's work. After a loss or a mistake people say qaddar allāh w mā shāʼ faʿal 'God decreed it, and did as He willed'. lō for advice, plans and wishes is fine.
dialogue: A
عندي عرض شغل في أبوظبي. شو رأيك؟
ʿindi ʿarẓ shughul fi Abūẓabi. shu raʼyak?
I've got a job offer in Abu Dhabi. What do you think?
B
ما شاء الله! لو أنا مكانك، جان وافقت على طول
mā shāʼ allāh! lō ana makānak, chān wāfagt ʿala ṭūl
That's great! If I were you, I'd say yes straight away.
A
بس أبوظبي بعيدة، وأهلي كلهم هني
bas Abūẓabi baʿīda, w ahli killhum hni
But Abu Dhabi's far, and all my family's here.
B
صح، بس هذي فرصة ما تتعوض
ṣaḥḥ, bas hādhi furṣa ma titʿawwaẓ
True, but this is a chance you won't get again.
A
لو أبوي يوافق، جان رحت
lō ubūy ywāfig, chān riḥt
If my dad agreed, I'd go.
B
كلمه انت. لو تشرح له، يمكن يوافق
kallmah inta. lō tishraḥ-lah, yimkin ywāfig
Talk to him yourself. If you explained it to him, he might agree.
A
يا ليت! إن شاء الله
yā lēt! in shāʼ allāh
I hope so! God willing.
B
وإذا رحت، أنا بزورك كل أسبوع!
w idha riḥt, ana bazūrak kill usbūʿ!
And if you go, I'll visit you every week!
items: if I were you (to a man)
to a woman: lō ana makānich (لو أنا مكانج)
a chance you won't get again, a once-in-a-lifetime chance
talk to him yourself, you talk to him (to a man)
to a woman: kallmīh inti (كلميه انتي)
if you explained (it) to him (to a man)
to a woman: lō tishraḥīn-lah (لو تشرحين له)
I wish, if only; I hope so
I'll visit you, I'll come and see you (to a man)

title: Even if it's just a little
goal: Try to leave Bū Rāshid's majlis before dinner, with Sēf there, and give in politely when he insists
tip: ḥatta lō means 'even if': ḥatta lō ʿindak imtiḥān 'even if you've got an exam'. Add ma for 'even if … not': ḥatta lō ma dhākart wāyid 'even if you haven't revised much'. w lō shwayy 'even just a little' is the host's favourite way to insist.
grammar: ḥatta lō 'even if' (ḥatta lō ʿindak …, ḥatta lō ma …)
culture: A Gulf host insists, often two or three times, and a guest usually says no at first. Giving in with zēn, bas shwayy 'OK, but just a little' honours the host. Sitting with the family for a few minutes counts; nobody expects you to eat a mountain of food.
dialogue: A
وين رايح يا ولدي؟ العشا جاهز!
wēn rāyiḥ yā wildi? il-ʿasha jāhiz!
Where are you off to, son? Dinner's ready!
B
السموحة يا عمي، لازم أروح. عندي امتحان باكر
is-samūḥa yā ʿammi, lāzim arūḥ. ʿindi imtiḥān bāchir
Forgive me, uncle, I have to go. I've got an exam tomorrow.
A
حتى لو عندك امتحان، لازم تتعشى ويانا
ḥatta lō ʿindak imtiḥān, lāzim titʿashsha wiyyāna
Even if you've got an exam, you must have dinner with us.
B
الله يخليك يا عمي، والله إني مستعجل
allāh ykhallīk yā ʿammi, wallāh inni mistaʿjil
Please, uncle, I'm honestly in a hurry.
A
ما يصير تطلع بلا عشا. ولو شوي!
ma yṣīr tiṭlaʿ bala ʿasha. w lō shwayy!
You can't leave without dinner. Even just a little!
B
زين، عشان خاطرك. بس شوي
zēn, ʿashān khāṭrak. bas shwayy
All right, for your sake. But just a little.
A
هذا الكلام! وحتى لو ما ذاكرت وايد، بتنجح إن شاء الله
hādha l-kalām! w ḥatta lō ma dhākart wāyid, bitinjaḥ in shāʼ allāh
That's more like it! And even if you haven't revised much, you'll pass, God willing.
B
آمين يا عمي
āmīn yā ʿammi
Amen, uncle.
items: UAE also, in older or Bedouin speech: ilā (إلى) for 'if'
ḥatta lō ma dhākart = even if you haven't revised
even just a little, even a bit
a host insisting: w lō shwayy!
ʿindi imtiḥān bāchir = I've got an exam tomorrow
bala = without: bala sukkar = without sugar
for your sake, just for you (to a man)
to a woman: ʿashān khāṭrich (عشان خاطرج)
that's more like it! now you're talking!
you'll pass, you'll do well (to a man)

title: He said he wants to see you
goal: Get back to your desk and let Maryam pass on messages: what the manager and two colleagues said
tip: To pass on what someone said, use gāl inn- or gālat inn- + an ending: gāl innah taʿbān 'he said he's not well', gālat innha fi ṭ-ṭarīg 'she said she's on her way'. -ah is 'he', -ha is 'she'. gāl-li innah is 'he told me (that) he'.
grammar: reported speech: gāl innah / gālat innha + what was said
dialogue: A
صباح الخير. المدير يسأل عنك
ṣabāḥ il-khēr. il-mudīr yisʼal ʿannak
Morning. The manager's been asking for you.
B
صباح النور. شو قال لج؟
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. shu gāl-lich?
Morning. What did he tell you?
A
قال إنه يبيك في مكتبه الساعة عشر
gāl innah yabīk fi maktabah is-sāʿa ʿashr
He said he wants to see you in his office at ten.
B
زين. وخالد مب هني اليوم؟
zēn. w Khālid mub hni l-yōm?
OK. And Khālid's not in today?
A
لا. دق علي وقال لي إنه تعبان
la. dagg ʿalay w gāl-li innah taʿbān
No. He rang me and told me he's not well.
B
سلامته! وسارة بعد؟
salāmtah! w Sāra baʿad?
I hope he's OK! And Sāra too?
A
لا، سارة قالت إنها في الطريق. زحمة وايد!
la, Sāra gālat innha fi ṭ-ṭarīg. zaḥma wāyid!
No, Sāra said she's on her way. The traffic's terrible!
B
زين، بروح للمدير. وإذا دق خالد، سلمي عليه
zēn, barūḥ lil-mudīr. w idha dagg Khālid, sallmī ʿalēh
OK, I'll go to the manager. And if Khālid rings, say hi to him for me.
items: he said (that) he, he said (that) it
about a woman: gālat innha (قالت إنها)
about a man: gāl innah (قال إنه)
she told me (that) she: gālat-li innha (قالت لي إنها)
what did he tell you? (to a woman)
to a man: shu gāl-lak? (شو قال لك؟)
in her office: fi maktab-ha (في مكتبها); not the same as maktaba 'library'
I hope he's all right, I hope he gets better (about a man who's ill)
if he rings, if he calls
if she rings: idha daggat (إذا دقت)
say hi to him (from me) (to a woman)
to a man: sallim ʿalēh (سلم عليه)

title: You told me you were flying today!
goal: Bump into Sēf at the mall when he thought you'd already left, and sort out who said what
tip: inn takes the same endings as nouns: inni 'that I', innak 'that you (m.)', innich 'that you (f.)', innah 'he', innha 'she', inna 'we', innkum 'you all', innhum 'they'. gilt-li innak msāfir 'you told me you were flying'. ʿala bāli innak … means 'I thought you …'.
grammar: inn- with every ending (inni, innak, inna): gilt-li innak msāfir
dialogue: A
هلا! انت هني؟ قلت لي إنك مسافر اليوم!
hala! inta hni? gilt-li innak msāfir il-yōm!
Hi! You're here? You told me you were flying today!
B
لا، قلت لك إني مسافر الخميس، مب اليوم!
la, gilt-lak inni msāfir il-khamīs, mub il-yōm!
No, I told you I'm flying on Thursday, not today!
A
صج؟ على بالي إنك رايح اليوم
ṣij? ʿala bāli innak rāyiḥ il-yōm
Really? I thought you were going today.
B
لا، فهمتني غلط. الحين أشتري هدايا حق أهلي
la, fhimtni ghalaṭ. il-ḥīn ashtiri hadāya ḥagg ahli
No, you got me wrong. Right now I'm buying presents for my family.
A
حلو! وأهلك يدرون إنك ياي؟
ḥilu! w ahlak yadrūn innak yāy?
Nice! And does your family know you're coming?
B
لا، أبيها مفاجأة. قلت لأخوي بس
la, abīha mufājaʼa. gilt l-akhūy bas
No, I want it to be a surprise. I've only told my brother.
A
زين. قول لهم إنا نسلم عليهم
zēn. gūl-lhum inna nsallim ʿalēhum
Great. Tell them we send our best.
B
إن شاء الله، أقول لهم. الله يسلمك
in shāʼ allāh, agūl-lhum. allāh ysallmak
I will, God willing. Thank you.

title: They say the manager's leaving
goal: Catch the latest office gossip from Maryam at work: what people are saying and what you've heard
tip: For news you've heard, start with simaʿt inn… 'I heard that…' or ygūlūn inn… 'they say that…'. Before a pronoun, inn takes its ending: simaʿt innah biytzawwaj 'I heard he's getting married'. To sound careful, add yimkin kalām bas 'maybe it's just talk' or allāhu aʿlam 'who knows'.
grammar: hearsay: ygūlūn inn…, simaʿt inn… (+ ending)
dialogue: A
سمعت إن المدير بيطلع من الشركة؟
simaʿt inn il-mudīr biyiṭlaʿ min ish-sharika?
Have you heard the manager's leaving the company?
B
لا! منو قال لج؟
la! minu gāl-lich?
No! Who told you?
A
كلهم يقولون إنه لقى شغل ثاني
killhum ygūlūn innah liga shughul thāni
Everyone's saying he's found another job.
B
صج؟ أنا سمعت إنه بيتزوج!
ṣij? ana simaʿt innah biytzawwaj!
Really? I heard he's getting married!
A
يمكن كلام بس. الله أعلم
yimkin kalām bas. allāhu aʿlam
Maybe it's just talk. Who knows.
B
بس إذا صج، منو بيصير المدير؟
bas idha ṣij, minu biyṣīr il-mudīr?
But if it's true, who's going to be manager?
A
يقولون إن أحمد بياخذ مكانه
ygūlūn inn Aḥmad biyākhidh makānah
They say Aḥmad will take his place.
B
أحمد؟! زين والله، هذا خبر حلو!
Aḥmad?! zēn wallāh, hādha khabar ḥilu!
Aḥmad?! Well, that's good news!
items: I heard (that); have you heard (that)…? (to a man)
to a woman: simaʿti inn (سمعتي إن)
about a woman: simaʿt innha (سمعت إنها)
yimkin kalām bas = maybe it's just talk
about a woman: bitiṭlaʿ min ish-sharika (بتطلع من الشركة)

title: Your uncle says come for dinner
goal: Pass on Bū Rāshid's message to Sēf: his greetings, his exact words and his dinner invitation
tip: Gulf speakers often quote straight, with no inn: gāl: idha ma yā, ana barūḥ-lah 'he said: if he doesn't come, I'll go to him'. ygūl-lak … passes a message on: ygūl-lak lēsh ma tzūrah? 'he says why don't you visit him?'. To send one back: gūl-lah inni yāy 'tell him I'm coming'.
grammar: passing on messages: direct quotes (gāl: …) and ygūl-lak 'he says (to tell you)'
culture: Greetings are passed on with care: if someone asks you to sallim ʿala…, it's polite to deliver it, and the reply to ysallim ʿalēk is allāh ysallmah. Older relatives expect visits and calls from the young; a message sent through a friend is a gentle reminder.
dialogue: A
شفت عمي في المجلس؟ شو قال لك؟
shift ʿammi fi l-majlis? shu gāl-lak?
Did you see my uncle at the majlis? What did he say to you?
B
هيه. يسلم عليك، ويقول لك ليش ما تزوره؟
hē. ysallim ʿalēk, w ygūl-lak lēsh ma tzūrah?
Yes. He says hi, and he says why don't you visit him?
A
الله يسلمه. والله مشغول هالأيام
allāh ysallmah. wallāh mashghūl hal-ayyām
God keep him. Honestly, I've been busy lately.
B
قال: العشا عندي يوم الجمعة، وسيف لازم ييي
gāl: il-ʿasha ʿindi yōm il-jumʿa, w Sēf lāzim yiyi
He said: "Dinner's at my place on Friday, and Sēf has to come."
A
يعني لازم أروح؟
yaʿni lāzim arūḥ?
So I have to go?
B
هيه! وقال: إذا ما يا، أنا بروح له
hē! w gāl: idha ma yā, ana barūḥ-lah
Yes! And he said: "If he doesn't come, I'll go to him."
A
عيل بروح! قول له إني ياي
ʿayal barūḥ! gūl-lah inni yāy
Then I'm going! Tell him I'm coming.
B
لا، دق عليه انت. يبي يسمع صوتك!
la, digg ʿalēh inta. yabi yismaʿ ṣōtak!
No, you ring him. He wants to hear your voice!
items: he says (to tell you), he's asking (to a man)
to a woman: ygūl-lich (يقول لج); she says: tgūl-lak (تقول لك)
why don't you visit him? (to a man)
to a woman: lēsh ma tzūrīnah? (ليش ما تزورينه؟)
busy lately, busy these days (a man)
at our place: il-ʿasha ʿindna (العشا عندنا)
if she doesn't come: idha ma yat (إذا ما يت)
to a woman: gūlī-lah inni (قولي له إني)
ring him, give him a call (to a man)
to a woman: diggī ʿalēh (دقي عليه)
he wants to hear your voice (to a man)
to a woman: yabi yismaʿ ṣōtich (يبي يسمع صوتج)

title: He said he was on his way
goal: Wait for Sēf with Fahad at a restaurant and report what Sēf told you on the phone
tip: Gulf Arabic keeps the speaker's tense when you report: Sēf said ana yāy, so you say gāl innah yāy 'he said he was coming'. 'I'll be there in ten minutes' becomes gāl innah biyōṣal baʿd ʿashr dagāyig. Only the person changes; English shifts the tense, Arabic doesn't.
grammar: no tense shift in reported speech (gāl innah yāy 'he said he was coming')
dialogue: A
وين سيف؟ مو قال إنه ياي الساعة سبع؟
wēn Sēf? mū gāl innah yāy is-sāʿa sabʿ?
Where's Sēf? Didn't he say he was coming at seven?
B
هيه، قال إنه في الطريق. يمكن زحمة
hē, gāl innah fi ṭ-ṭarīg. yimkin zaḥma
Yes, he said he was on his way. Maybe it's the traffic.
A
شنو قال لك بعد؟
shinu gāl-lak baʿad?
What else did he tell you?
B
قال: أنا طالع من البيت الحين
gāl: ana ṭāliʿ min il-bēt il-ḥīn
He said: "I'm leaving the house now."
A
ومتى قال جذي؟
w mita gāl chidhi?
And when did he say that?
B
قبل ساعة! وقال إنه بيوصل بعد عشر دقايق
gabil sāʿa! w gāl innah biyōṣal baʿd ʿashr dagāyig
An hour ago! And he said he'd be here in ten minutes.
A
هذا سيف! يقول إنه ياي، واهو للحين في البيت!
hādha Sēf! ygūl innah yāy, w ihu lil-ḥīn fi l-bēt!
That's Sēf for you! He says he's coming, and he's still at home!
B
خلني أدق عليه وأشوف
khallni adigg ʿalēh w ashūf
Let me ring him and see.
items: he said he was coming, he said he's on his way
about a woman: gālat innha yāya (قالت إنها ياية)
he said he'd get here, he said he'll arrive
about a woman: gālat innha bitōṣal (قالت إنها بتوصل)

he said so, he said that

leaving the house, heading out (a man)
a woman: ṭālʿa min il-bēt (طالعة من البيت)
